title: 1. Subject-Verb Agreement & Sentence Foundations (1/2)
group: Module 1 · The Foundational Zero-to-Hero Grammar Engine
blocks: The building blocks of a sentence and the eight agreement cases that decide your mark. The single highest-value, lowest-effort accuracy gain in the whole exam.

Before any IELTS-specific technique, your sentences have to be mechanically sound. This module fixes the four faults that quietly lower your score on every single line of your writing and speaking: verbs that do not agree with their subjects, tenses that put events in the wrong time, missing or misused articles, and wrong prepositions. None of these is difficult. All of them are habits. Module 1 turns the correct habit into your default, so that by Module 2 you can build ambitious sentences on a base that does not leak marks.
1.1 First, the building blocks (start here even if you think you know)

This book assumes you know nothing, so we begin with the parts of a sentence. You do not need to memorise these labels to speak Bangla, but almost every rule in this book is stated using them, so learn to recognise them.
Every basic English sentence has two essential parts and often a third:
The subject is the person or thing the sentence is about, the one that does the action. In “Students study hard,” the subject is students.
The verb is the action or the state of being. In “Students study hard,” the verb is study. The verb be (is, am, are, was, were) shows a state rather than an action: “The graph is clear.”
The object is the person or thing that receives the action. In “Students use the internet,” the object is the internet.
The normal English order is Subject + Verb + Object (S + V + O). Students (S) use (V) the internet (O).

Bangla is a Subject-Object-Verb language. আমি ভাত খাই is literally “I rice eat,” with the verb at the very end. English puts the verb second, right after the subject: “I eat rice.” When an English sentence you write feels wrong, the first thing to check is whether the verb has drifted to the end out of Bangla habit.

“Agreement” simply means matching. Subject-verb agreement is the rule that the verb must match its subject in number. A singular subject (one) takes one form of the verb; a plural subject (more than one) takes another. That is the entire idea. The rest of this chapter is about the cases where spotting the true subject is tricky.
In the present simple tense, the verb changes depending on whether the subject is singular or plural.
Notice the trap that catches thousands of Bangladeshi candidates: the -s is reversed between nouns and verbs.
On a noun, -s means plural: one student, many students.
On a verb, -s means singular: he works, they work.
So a correct sentence often has an -s on either the noun or the verb, but not both: The student works. (singular noun, verb takes -s) / The students work. (plural noun, verb has no -s)
The verb be and have are irregular and must be memorised:
The result is clear. / The results are clear. The number has risen. / The numbers have risen.

title: 1. Subject-Verb Agreement & Sentence Foundations (2/2)
group: Module 1 · The Foundational Zero-to-Hero Grammar Engine
blocks: 1.3 The cases that actually decide your mark

The core rule is easy. Marks are lost on the cases below, where the true subject is hidden, disguised, or further away from the verb than a nearer noun. Master these eight and you remove almost every agreement error from your writing.
Case 1 · Words between the subject and the verb
The verb agrees with the true subject, never with the nearest noun. Writers are pulled toward the closest word, which is usually wrong.
The list of items are on the table.
The list of items is on the table.
The subject is “list” (singular), not “items”. Cross out the middle phrase and the truth is obvious: “The list … is.”
The quality of the answers were poor.
The quality of the answers was poor.
Technique: find the subject, then mentally delete every word between it and the verb. “The list of items is.”
Case 2 · “The number of” versus “a number of”
This pair appears constantly in Writing Task 1, and the two behave in opposite ways.
“The number of + plural noun” takes a singular verb (the subject is number, one figure).
“A number of + plural noun” takes a plural verb (it simply means several).
The number of tourists has increased since 2010. / A number of tourists were waiting outside the museum.
Words such as government, team, committee, family, company, public, staff name a group. In IELTS academic writing, treat each as a single unit and use a singular verb.
The government is planning three new policies. / The committee has reached a decision.

(British English sometimes allows a plural verb when the focus is on the individual members: “the team are arguing among themselves.” For IELTS academic Writing, stay singular and consistent. It is safer and never wrong.)
Each, every, everyone, everybody, someone, anyone, nobody, either, neither, one are all singular, however plural the words around them look.
Each of the students has a laptop. (not “have”) / Everyone in the classes was present. / Neither of the options is acceptable.
With these paired connectors, the verb agrees with the nearer subject, the one closest to the verb.

Neither the manager nor the employees were informed. (nearer subject: employees, plural) / Neither the employees nor the manager was informed. (nearer subject: manager, singular) / Not only the students but also the teacher was worried.
Two subjects joined by and are almost always plural.
The teacher and the students were in the hall. / Poverty and unemployment remain serious problems.
Exception: when the two words describe a single combined thing, treat them as singular: “Bread and butter is a common breakfast.” This is rare in IELTS.
After there, the verb agrees with the real subject, which comes after the verb.
There is a serious problem. (subject: problem, singular) / There are several factors. (subject: factors, plural) / There is a range of options. (subject: range, singular)
Case 8 · Uncountable nouns, amounts, and inverted structures

Uncountable nouns are treated as singular and never take a plural -s. Memorise the high-frequency IELTS set as a block: information, advice, knowledge, research, equipment, furniture, accommodation, traffic, progress, news, money, water, work.
The informations are correct and he gave many advices.
The information is correct and he gave a lot of advice.
Amounts of time, money, and distance are treated as a single quantity, so they take a singular verb. Ten years is a long time to wait. / Five thousand taka is not enough.

Inverted structures (where the verb comes before the subject) still agree with the subject. When a sentence begins with a negative adverb such as not only or hardly, find the subject after the verb and match it. Hardly ever does the government reverse such a decision. / Only after 2010 did the figures begin to fall.
(You will meet inversion in full in Chapter 8. Here, only notice that agreement still applies.)
Why Bangla speakers make agreement mistakes

Almost every subject-verb agreement error you make traces back to one fact: the Bangla verb does not change its ending to match a singular or plural subject the way the English verb does. The verb form যায় (jay) is identical for “he” and for “they.” Bangla marks person and formality, but it does not force the singular-plural switch on the verb that English demands. Because your first language never trained this switch, your ear does not warn you when it is missing.

Error type 1 · The dropped third-person -s. Because Bangla adds no -s, learners write the base verb everywhere.
✗ He go to the market every day. / The population increase rapidly.
✓ He goes to the market every day. / The population increases rapidly.

Error type 2 · The dropped or wrong “is / are.” Bangla often has no separate word for is in a simple statement (সে ভালো = “he good”), so learners drop it or pick the wrong number.
✗ Many people is using the internet. / The graph show that pollution have increased.
✓ Many people are using the internet. / The graph shows that pollution has increased.
Why this one rule caps your band

Subject-verb agreement is the error examiners notice first, because it appears in the very first line of almost every answer and it repeats. A script with recurring agreement errors cannot reach Band 7 in Grammatical Range and Accuracy, however good the ideas are, because the criterion at Band 7 requires that the majority of sentences are error-free. One agreement slip per sentence removes that. The damage is heaviest in Writing Task 1, which lives on subjects like the number of, the proportion of, the figure for, every one of which is singular. Fixing agreement is the single highest-value, lowest-effort accuracy gain in the whole exam.

Skills: Writing, Speaking
Task 1: The number of visitors has risen sharply, whereas the proportion of local tourists has fallen.
Task 2: Although the government provides free healthcare, demand continues to outstrip supply.
Speaking Part 2: My family lives in a small town, and each of my brothers has a different job.
End of Chapter 1. Chapter 2 (Tense Mastery & Time Precision) follows.

title: 1. Practice · Subject-Verb Agreement & Sentence Foundations
group: Module 1 · The Foundational Zero-to-Hero Grammar Engine
blocks: The verb must match its subject in number, not the nearest noun. Singular subjects take the -s form of the verb; plural subjects don't. Get this one reflex right and you remove the most common agreement error in your writing.
**Why it matters:** Subject-verb agreement is checked on every single sentence you write, so one bad habit here costs marks over and over.
In the present simple, a **singular subject** (he, she, it, one thing) takes the verb **+ s/es**: the student works.
A **plural subject** takes the **base verb**, no -s: the students work.
The -s is reversed between nouns and verbs: on a noun, -s means plural; on a verb, -s means singular. A correct sentence rarely has -s on both.
The result is clear vs the results are clear; the number has risen vs the numbers have risen.

blocks.title: Exercise 1.1 · Identification and Correction
blocks.instructions: Each sentence below contains a subject-verb agreement error, except three, which are already correct. Rewrite each faulty sentence correctly, and for the correct ones write “Correct.” Do this with a pen before checking the key.

items.prompt: The list of approved candidates are posted on the noticeboard.
items.answer: The list of approved candidates is posted on the noticeboard.
accepted: The list of approved candidates is posted on the noticeboard.
items.reason: Subject is “list” (singular), not “candidates.”

items.prompt: Each of the students have submitted their assignment.
items.answer: Each of the students has submitted his or her assignment.
accepted: Each of the students has submitted his or her assignment.
Each of the students has submitted their assignment.
items.reason: “Each of” is always singular.

items.prompt: The government are introducing a new tax next year.
items.answer: The government is introducing a new tax next year.
accepted: The government is introducing a new tax next year.
items.reason: Collective noun as one unit takes a singular verb in academic writing.

items.prompt: Neither the teacher nor the students was ready for the test.
items.answer: Neither the teacher nor the students were ready for the test.
accepted: Neither the teacher nor the students were ready for the test.
items.reason: With “neither…nor,” the verb agrees with the nearer subject, “students” (plural).

items.prompt: The number of accidents on this road have increased.
items.answer: The number of accidents on this road has increased.
accepted: The number of accidents on this road has increased.
items.reason: “The number of” is singular.

items.prompt: There is several reasons for this decline.
items.answer: There are several reasons for this decline.
accepted: There are several reasons for this decline.
items.reason: The real subject “reasons” is plural.

items.prompt: A large amount of information were collected during the survey.
items.answer: A large amount of information was collected during the survey.
accepted: A large amount of information was collected during the survey.
items.reason: “Information” is uncountable and singular, so “amount … was.”

items.prompt: Ten kilometres are a long way to walk in the heat.
items.answer: Ten kilometres is a long way to walk in the heat.
accepted: Ten kilometres is a long way to walk in the heat.
items.reason: A single distance is treated as one quantity: singular verb.

items.prompt: The committee has agreed on the final budget.
items.answer: Correct.
accepted: Correct.
Correct
The committee has agreed on the final budget.
items.reason: “Committee” as one unit takes the singular “has.”

items.prompt: The quality of the roads in rural areas are very poor.
items.answer: The quality of the roads in rural areas is very poor.
accepted: The quality of the roads in rural areas is very poor.
items.reason: Subject is “quality” (singular), not “roads” or “areas.”

items.prompt: Poverty and illiteracy remains major obstacles to development.
items.answer: Poverty and illiteracy remain major obstacles to development.
accepted: Poverty and illiteracy remain major obstacles to development.
items.reason: Two subjects joined by “and” are plural.

items.prompt: Everyone in the two classes were given a certificate.
items.answer: Everyone in the two classes was given a certificate.
accepted: Everyone in the two classes was given a certificate.
items.reason: “Everyone” is singular.

items.prompt: Not only the manager but also the workers is unhappy with the plan.
items.answer: Not only the manager but also the workers are unhappy with the plan.
accepted: Not only the manager but also the workers are unhappy with the plan.
items.reason: With “not only…but also,” the verb agrees with the nearer subject, “workers” (plural).

items.prompt: The data collected over ten years show a clear pattern.
items.answer: Correct.
accepted: Correct.
Correct
The data collected over ten years show a clear pattern.
items.reason: “Data” is treated as a plural or mass noun; “the data … show” is acceptable and consistent here.

items.prompt: My knowledge of these topics are limited.
items.answer: My knowledge of these topics is limited.
accepted: My knowledge of these topics is limited.
items.reason: “Knowledge” is uncountable and singular; subject is “knowledge,” not “topics.”

items.prompt: A number of students has failed to register on time.
items.answer: A number of students have failed to register on time.
accepted: A number of students have failed to register on time.
items.reason: “A number of” means “several” and takes a plural verb.

items.prompt: The population of the coastal cities have grown rapidly.
items.answer: The population of the coastal cities has grown rapidly.
accepted: The population of the coastal cities has grown rapidly.
items.reason: Subject is “population” (singular), not “cities.”

items.prompt: Neither of the two proposals seem practical.
items.answer: Neither of the two proposals seems practical.
accepted: Neither of the two proposals seems practical.
items.reason: “Neither” is singular.

items.prompt: Statistics is a subject that many students find difficult.
items.answer: Correct.
accepted: Correct.
Correct
Statistics is a subject that many students find difficult.
items.reason: “Statistics” as the name of a subject is singular: “statistics is.”

items.prompt: The equipment in the laboratories need to be replaced.
items.answer: The equipment in the laboratories needs to be replaced.
accepted: The equipment in the laboratories needs to be replaced.
items.reason: “Equipment” is uncountable and singular.

blocks: Most agreement errors don't come from the core rule -- they come from eight disguised cases where the real subject is hidden, delayed, or joined to another noun. Learn these eight and almost every agreement mistake in your essays disappears.
**Why it matters:** The core rule is easy; marks are lost on the cases where the true subject is hard to spot.
The cases that decide your mark
**Words between subject and verb:** ignore them -- the verb agrees with the true subject, not the nearest noun.
**"The number of" (singular) vs "a number of" (plural):** the number of tourists has increased, but a number of tourists were waiting.
**Collective nouns** (government, team, committee): singular in IELTS academic writing.
**Indefinite pronouns** (each, everyone, neither) are always singular.
**"Neither...nor", "either...or"**: the verb agrees with the nearer subject.
**"There is / there are"**: agrees with what comes after the verb.
**Uncountable nouns and amounts** (information, ten years): singular, even though they look plural.

blocks.title: Exercise 1.2 · IELTS Essay Editing
blocks.instructions: The paragraph below is from a Band 5.5 Task 2 essay. It contains ten subject-verb agreement errors. Find them, then rewrite the whole paragraph correctly.

items.prompt: Nowadays, the number of people who works from home have increased dramatically. There is many reasons for this change. First, technology allow employees to stay connected from anywhere. Second, each of the major companies now offer flexible arrangements. However, some managers believes that productivity fall when staff is not in the office. In my opinion, the advantages of remote work outweighs the disadvantages, and this trend are likely to continue.
items.answer: Nowadays, the number of people who work from home has increased dramatically. There are many reasons for this change. First, technology allows employees to stay connected from anywhere. Second, each of the major companies now offers flexible arrangements. However, some managers believe that productivity falls when staff are not in the office. In my opinion, the advantages of remote work outweigh the disadvantages, and this trend is likely to continue.
accepted: Nowadays, the number of people who work from home has increased dramatically. There are many reasons for this change. First, technology allows employees to stay connected from anywhere. Second, each of the major companies now offers flexible arrangements. However, some managers believe that productivity falls when staff are not in the office. In my opinion, the advantages of remote work outweigh the disadvantages, and this trend is likely to continue.
items.reason: Ten agreement errors: who works→work; have increased→has increased (the number is singular); There is→There are; technology allow→allows; each of … offer→offers; managers believes→believe; productivity fall→falls; staff is→staff are; advantages … outweighs→outweigh; this trend are→is.
